reason: Create account is a menuitem in the Add account menu, which uses a roving tabindex, so Tab skips its items by design. From the keyboard, Tab reaches the Add account button, Enter opens the menu and moves focus onto the Create account menuitem (the element the sweep measured), and Enter on it opens the Create account dialog with focus inside it. The sweep started with the menu already open from a mouse click and Tabbed away from it, so it never took the keyboard path.

The Review button belongs to step one of the Make a credit payment dialog (accounts.pay-credit), not to the review state, where it no longer exists. There Tab reaches Review on the fourth stop, and Enter swaps the same dialog to the review step with Edit and Confirm payment, which Tab then reaches. Review opens no second dialog, so the check's premise is wrong and the keyboard path works.

On both states the sweep pressed Enter and Space on the tab-stop wrapper div around the Transfer split button, which has no action. The real trigger is the Open Menu chevron button, the next Tab stop (stop 45 on the checking account, stop 42 on Treasury): there Enter and Space each open the Transfer in and Transfer out menu and move focus onto Transfer in, and Escape returns focus to the chevron.

On accounts.credit, Tab stop 39 is the tooltip-anchor div around the button, and Enter on it opens nothing, which is where the sweep pressed its keys. The next stop is the Request a limit increase button itself, and Enter on it opens the Request a credit limit increase dialog (URL gains action=requestLimitChange) and moves focus onto the dialog.

In the share dialog one Tab puts focus in the Recipient emails combobox, aria-expanded flips from false to true on focus and the three suggestions (jason@green.com, aliyah@mcmahon.com, jordi@mercury.com) show; ArrowDown then moves aria-activedescendant to the first option. Enter and Space had nothing to open because the list was already open, so the listbox does not need a mouse.
